newsitem.title: JAPAN: TENNIS-GRAF CONTINUES REBOUND WITH WIN OVER MAJOLI.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF CONTINUES REBOUND WITH WIN OVER MAJOLI.

text.p: World number one Steffi Graf powered past Croatia's Iva Majoli 6-2 6-3 on Friday to stay on course for a showdown with 16-year-old Swiss Martina Hingis in Sunday's final.
Hingis, the Australian Open champion, easily defeated South Africa's Amanda Coetzer 6-0 6-1. Coetzer lost to France's Mary Pierce in the Australian Open semifinals.
Top seed Graf, who last week was knocked out of the Australian Open in the fourth round and then saw her father convicted of tax evasion, finished off fifth seed Majoli in just 55 minutes.
Defending champion Majoli started out well, holding her own with Graf until the sixth game of the first set, when the relentless Graf's power turned the tide in her favour.
"The match had some really good rallies," Graf told reporters. "I'm happy about the match."
Asked to compare herself to the second-seeded Hingis, who on Friday won her 100th victory on the Women's Tennis Association tour, Graf, 26, said age was the main difference.
"Obviously 10 years makes a big difference. You're young, there's more excitement, you've got nothing to lose," she said.
"Ten years later, you're a different person. You're not as naive or as open-minded as you were 10 years ago."

Hingis, the second seed, played aggressively and forced Coetzer all over the court on her way to victory in only 45 minutes, told reporters: "I just felt very confident today. I was playing very even."
In Saturday's semifinal, Graf will play eighth-seeded Brenda Schultz-McCarthy of the Netherlands, who beat Spain's Conchita Martinez 6-1, 6-0.
Hingis will square off against Germany's Anke Huber, who defeated American Lindsay Davenport 6-3, 4-6, 6-2.
